# package dbc

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-canbus/dbc"
```

Package dbc reads and writes DBC files into the format-independent model of package candb.

Supported: VERSION, BU\_, VAL\_TABLE\_, BO\_ and SG\_ (Intel and Motorola, signed and unsigned, scaling, limits, units, receivers, simple and extended multiplexing), BO\_TX\_BU\_, CM\_ for the network, nodes, messages and signals, BA\_DEF\_ / BA\_DEF\_DEF\_ / BA\_ for the network, nodes, messages and signals, VAL\_, SIG\_VALTYPE\_ (float and double signals), SG\_MUL\_VAL\_ and SIG\_GROUP\_. The attributes GenMsgCycleTime, GenSigStartValue, VFrameFormat and CANFD\_BRS are also mapped onto the model's cycle time, initial value and CAN FD flags.

Everything else (environment variables, signal types, relation attributes, categories, filters) is skipped with a warning diagnostic; nothing is dropped silently. There is no public specification of the format: behaviour follows the de facto Vector conventions and is cross-checked against cantools and canmatrix (see INTEROPERABILITY.md).

## Variables

```go
var ErrName = errors.New("dbc: name is not a DBC identifier")
```

ErrName reports a name [Write](#func-write) cannot write: DBC writes the names of nodes, value tables, messages, signals, senders, receivers, multiplexer switches and signal groups as bare identifiers, so they must be DBC identifiers (a letter, '\_' or a byte from 0x80 up, then those or digits); node and receiver names must not be DBC keywords either. Names from KCD or ARXML may be any text.

## Functions

### func Parse

```go
func Parse(r io.Reader) (*candb.Database, []candb.Diagnostic, error)
```

Parse parses DBC source. It returns the database, every diagnostic (info, warnings and errors, sorted by line) and, when any diagnostic is an error, a \*[ParseError](#type-parseerror): the database then describes only what could be parsed and validated.

### func ParseBytes

```go
func ParseBytes(src []byte) (*candb.Database, []candb.Diagnostic, error)
```

ParseBytes parses DBC source held in memory. See [Parse](#func-parse).

### func ParseFile

```go
func ParseFile(path string) (*candb.Database, []candb.Diagnostic, error)
```

ParseFile parses a DBC file. See [Parse](#func-parse).

### func Write

```go
func Write(w io.Writer, db *candb.Database) error
```

Write writes db as a DBC file. The model's cycle times, initial values and CAN FD flags are written as the attributes GenMsgCycleTime, GenSigStartValue, VFrameFormat and CANFD\_BRS when the database does not carry them already. Multiplexing is written with mN indicators and, when it is not simple (more than one switch or ranges), SG\_MUL\_VAL\_.

Every name written as an identifier is checked first; when one is not a DBC identifier, Write writes nothing and returns an error wrapping ErrName. Strings (comments, units, value descriptions, attributes) are quoted and escaped.

## Types

### type ParseError

```go
type ParseError struct {
	Diagnostics []candb.Diagnostic
}
```

ParseError reports a DBC file that could not be parsed without errors. The database and every diagnostic are still returned by [Parse](#func-parse).

#### func (ParseError) Error

```go
func (e *ParseError) Error() string
```

Error reports the first error diagnostic and how many there are.
